messages:
jamie: thanks everyone for staying after the all-hands. wanted to capture the follow-ups on runway and procurement so folks who couldn't stay can catch up.

nina: quick one — what exactly was the runway number again? slides showed two scenarios.

elaine: short answer: ~18 months under the baseline plan (no aggressive Dedicated commitments). the downside scenario with hiring ramp and slower revenue puts us around 14 months.

sam: to clarify, baseline assumes moderate sales ramp and the hiring pause levers we discussed (hiring freeze for non-critical roles in Q3).

matt: numbers detail: current gross burn ~ $5.4M/mo, expected net burn falls to ~ $3.2M/mo by EOY assuming sales targets. i'll post the forecast model.

jamie: @matt please share the model (view only) and call out which hires are considered critical.

matt: here's the sheet: https://short.link/redwood-fin-2026 (view only). Critical hires: 2 infra SWE-SRE, 1 security engineer, 2 AEs. everything else is deferrable or backfill.

olivia: procurement question: new thresholds? vendor onboarding slowness flagged by integrations team.

devon: new approval rules starting next week: purchases >= $10k need finance + cost-owner approval; >= $50k needs exec sponsor. standard SLA is 3 business days; new vendor onboarding up to 7 days.

nina: we have a partner onboarding that can't wait 7 days. any expedited path?

devon: yes — tag @devon and @finance-bot with "expedite" on the PO form; we aim for 48-72 hours for urgent vendor requests, legal and security still required.

jamie: can you paste the PO form fields so teams know what to fill?

devon: snippet:
```
PO Request fields: vendor_name, amount, cost_center, justification, contract_term, contact_person, expedited_flag
Approvals: cost-owner -> finance -> exec (if >=50k)
Target SLA: 3 business days standard, 48-72 hrs if expedited
```

matt: another procurement-related note: Dedicated reserved capacity remains on the roadmap but any new large commits must include a 9-12 month ROI business case.

olivia: can we get a one-pager template for that business case? engineering needs the assumptions (throughput lift, ops savings).

matt: yes — i'll share a one-pager with expected throughput uplift, cost per token comparison, quantization/ops savings assumptions, and break-even term.

sam: transparency request: can finance publish a monthly snapshot of top spend categories and runway sensitivity? would help teams prioritize.

matt: will publish a monthly dashboard in #finance and pin a summary in #all-hands: top vendors, committed reserved spend, forecast burn sensitivity to hires and deals.

jamie: cards question: default procurement card limits? any temporary increases allowed?

elaine: default card limit is $5k. team leads can request temporary increases via the PO workflow; approvals based on cost center and spend history.

nina: will the one-pager include quantization and caching savings so infra proposals can be realistic?

matt: yes, ops savings and estimated token-cost reductions via batching/KV caching will be included.

jamie: final ask — can leadership post a short FAQ with the threshold bullets and runway recap for folks who missed the tail of the meeting?

elaine: yes — i'll post a pinned FAQ and a 3-min Loom explaining the new procurement flow.

finance-bot: Procurement workflow updated 2026-03-23T15:10:00Z. Use /po-request to start. :robot_face:

jamie: great, thanks everyone. closing thread. :slightly_smiling_face:
